answer: The strongest cheap check I know is Proof of unique postal address history with postal service attestation. It demands an address the postal service delivered to across years, and the ledge is that the proof is bound to one body, one device, one history. The verifier never sees the raw secret, only a proof that an address the postal service delivered to across years — so privacy survives, and the prism is that a stolen database buys the attacker nothing at all. One clone is cheap; a hundred are a small business with no revenue. The ocean is the point where the farm's spreadsheet turns red.
